Below are instructions to help you navigate the different functions within Digital Collections.

Browse all

Click on the browse link from the homepage to view all the images across all collections simultaneously. The browse link is also available from the main menu at the top of each page.

Browse collections

In addition to using the narrow/refine search option, you can view all the images in a particular collection from their individual collection information page. Visit the homepage and select the collection that you are interested in, and then click on the 'browse' button at the bottom of the collection landing page.

Simple search

Digital Collections provides a simple search box in the top right-hand corner of every web page. This searches across all fields, in all collections, and for all terms that you put in the search box, in any order when done from the home page. An asterisk (*) can be used to replace characters at the end of a search term, for example, hair* will return records for hair, hairdresser, hairdressing, hairstyle etc.

Advanced search

The advanced search enables you to build a more complex search query on selected fields/collections. For example, when searching for works by a particular photographer, you can use the advanced search to specify the search field as 'creator' and only find the works by that specific photographer. You can also narrow your search by using multiple search terms targeted to specific fields. The simple search box searches across all of the fields and will find any items that have a connection to the photographer, regardless of whether they were created by that photographer or not.

Advanced search types

The advanced search offers some additional search types: Search Terms:

  • all of the words - this searches for all the words that you enter in the search box, in any order (this is the same as the simple search);
  • exact phrase - searches for all of the words in the exact order;
  • any of the words - searches for any of the words entered in the search box, so a search for 'Bernard Leach' will find records which contain 'Bernard' but not 'Leach', and vice versa, as well as records containing both words;
  • none of the words - use this option in combination with any of the other search options, in order to exclude a term.
Date:
  • on- this searches for records that has that specific date within it;
  • after- the search will provide records with material dated after the date provided and does not include the date provided;
  • before- the search will provide records with material dated before the date provided and does not include the date provided;
  • between- the search will provide records with dates between the ones provided. For example: 1983 and 1985 will result in material from 1983, 1984, and 1985.

Searching within a Collection

When browsing a collection, not your search results, you will use the search bar in the top right to perform searches. This will search just the specific collection you are currently browsing. If you need to use the advanced search feature when browsing a collection, click advanced search under the search bar. In the left column there will be a list of collections as well as the option to Select All Collections. Deselect this option and click on the box associated with the collection you want to perform an advanced search within.

Displaying search results

Click on the 'list view' icon or 'grid view' icon at the top of the search results pages to change how the thumbnail images are displayed. The 'list view' will display additional information about the items such as creator, digital collection, subject and/or description whereas the 'grid view' allows you to view more images on the page at once. You can also increase the number of results shown on each page using the drop down to the right of the list and grid view buttons. You can display 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200 results at a time.

Sorting search results

You can use the drop-down menu at the top of the page (the 'sort' button on a mobile device) to change the order in which your results are displayed. The default order is based on relevance, which is determined by the frequency and distribution of matching keywords in each record compared to others. Matches in the title or subject fields are given more relevancy weight. You can change this order to sort alphabetically by either the title, subject or description. When searching within a specific collection, there may be additional sorting options.

Narrowing your search

On the search results pages or when browsing within a collection, use the terms in the far-left column to narrow your search further. These are called facets. If you are using a mobile device, you will need to click on the 'refine' button. You can narrow your search to particular collections, as well as narrowing results to a particular subject, creator, date, type (still image, text, sound or moving image) or format (jpeg, tiff, pdf, mp4 etc). Each collection has a customized list of facets to enhance your search experience.

Searching within a record

When looking through an item record, there may be multiple pages shown in the table on the right. At the top of that table, there is a search bar. This searches the metadata records on a page level as well as any OCR provided.

Search results within an item

When looking through a single page item, search results are shown as highlights within the metadata. If the single page item is text based and the search term is within the OCR, click to enlarge the image using the arrow in the top right corner of the image. The image will then appear in a pop-up and search terms will be highlighted within the image itself.

When looking through a multi-page item, there is a table on the right with thumbnails for the pages. If the search term is on that page, a red bar will show to the left of that thumbnail. If the search term is in the metadata, it will be highlighted. If the search term is within the OCR of the image itself, click the arrow in the top right corner of the image. The image will then appear in a pop-up and search terms will be highlighted within the image itself.

Image zoom

Several image collections can be zoomed to see the images in significantly more detail. To enlarge the image to its maximum size, click on the arrow in the top right corner of the image. The image will then appear in a pop-up, where it can be enlarged or rotated.

Download images

Click on the 'download' icon on the top right of each individual image record page to download the image to your computer. You can download an image up to a maximum size and a textual document as a pdf. Most items within Digital Collections you can download though there are notable exceptions such as the Atlanta Journal- Constitution Photographs.

Click on the 'print' icon on the top right of each image record page to print the image and its description.

Saved items

You can save images to a personal saved items page where you can export a list of those items or share links to them with others. Click '☆ save' on the search results pages, or individual image record pages, to save an item. You can access the saved items from the main menu at the top of each page. Please note that the saved items are kept in the browser cache of your computer/device, so they will not be accessible from another machine unless you save them as a link, or if you register for an account through worldcat.org and login to save the items. The links you create will be permanent, but you cannot modify the set of items for a link once the link is created. If you are working on a public computer, click on 'remove' to clear all saved items before leaving the machine. You can also clear saved items by deleting the browser cache.
